citations.quote: To evaluate the impact of the CA property under network conditions that are favorable to the attacker,we assume a single network delay setting of 10 seconds between honest nodes, while the attacker is assumed to have negligible block propagation and reception delay.
citations.supports: Network setting: 10 s honest delay, zero-delay attacker

citations.quote: We simulate a network consisting of 100 miners.
citations.supports: 100 miners with equal honest hash power; attacker pool of 100*alpha miners

citations.quote: The block generation time is fixed at 600 seconds, consistent with Bitcoin.
Each simulation terminates when the main chain reaches 100,000 blocks.
This action creates a fork, forcing a fraction of the honest network to waste hash power on a chain that the attacker intends to obsolete.

permitted_edits.purpose: add a per-block random hash plus pool/published flags used by the tie-breaks and the attacker
new: Smallest-Hash and CA+Smallest-Hash comparison of two tips (Algorithm 1 of the paper)
new: reduced network model (10 s honest delay, zero-delay pool), per-node fork choice, pool merging and the L-stubborn policy; writes the main-chain ledger
new: delayed block delivery task for the direct-broadcast model

hook at the top of main() that runs the model for mode codes 1/3/4 and writes blockList.txt with attacker blocks labelled Orphan (orphan_rate = attacker revenue share); the line that sets the seed is kept untouched

question: With an L-stubborn attacker holding hash-power share alpha in {0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4} against 10 s honest propagation delay and a zero-delay attacker, how does the attacker's main-chain revenue share differ between the Smallest-Hash tie-break and CA+Smallest-Hash, and does it match Figure 5 of the paper (profitable above y=alpha under Small, roughly at/below y=alpha under CA+Small)?
rationale:
VERSION CHANGE vs. the approved v1 (10,000 blocks): after implementing the edits I timed them in the sandbox. One run with 100 miners and 100,000 blocks takes about 0.6 s wall time including javac (8 runs at 100,000 blocks took 4.7 s in total; the simulation loop itself is ~0.03 s per 10,000 blocks). So the paper's own block count (100,000) is affordable: 40 formal runs + 3 validation runs ~ 30 s. END_BLOCK_HEIGHT is therefore raised from 10,000 to the paper's 100,000, which removes the block-count difference as a source of disagreement. Also: Node.java is NOT changed (the reduced model lives in the new StubbornAttacker/ForkChoice/DeliverBlockTask files and a small hook at the top of Main.main), so it is dropped from the permitted edits.

METRIC REDEFINITION (agreed with the researcher): SimBlock's card allows only t90_ms and orphan_rate (SB card, Metrics), so attacker revenue cannot be a plan metric. In this experiment the edited code writes blockList.txt as a ledger of main-chain blocks only (genesis excluded, last 10 blocks dropped as unsettled), labelling blocks mined by the attacker pool 'Orphan' and honest blocks 'OnChain'. Hence the reported orphan_rate = attacker blocks on the main chain / main-chain blocks = the paper's attacker revenue RR_attacker (Eq. 1). It is NOT a real orphan rate; the report and figures will say so.

WHY SIMBLOCK: the paper itself used SimBlock (Sec. 6.1). SimBlock is a node-level PoW simulator with forks and orphans (SB-M3, SB-M4) and per-node chain tips; BlockSim has a single global chain decided at the end of a run (BS-M3) and no per-node fork choice or topology (BS-N1), so per-node Small/CA tie-breaks cannot be expressed there. Both simulators lack attacker strategies (SB-N1, BS-N2), so L-stubborn and the CA rule are added by permitted edits (SB-S1, SB-S3).

HONEST DISCLOSURE: the edit is large. SimBlock's regional gossip / CBR / churn network and its Timer are bypassed in this experiment (SB-M1/SB-M2 are not used); only SimBlock's Block class, its Main entry point/seed/ledger output, and its PoW exponential block-time model (mean INTERVAL, difficulty fixed) are reused. This follows the paper's own simplified network assumption (a single 10 s delay between honest nodes, zero-delay attacker).

WHAT IS ADDED: (1) a per-block random 64-bit hash (Main.random, so the harness seed controls it); (2) ForkChoice: longest chain; equal height -> Smallest-Hash (smaller tip hash wins) or CA+Smallest-Hash (walk both tips back to the last common ancestor and compare the hashes of the two blocks just above it, Algorithm 1 of the paper); every honest node keeps its own tip; (3) an L-stubborn pool: it withholds blocks; when an honest block raises the public height to h and the pool's private height is >= h it releases only the private blocks up to height h (lead>=2: reveal one block, state k -> (k-1)'; lead 1: publish -> 0'); when it is behind it abandons its branch (no trial-stubbornness); a block mined in tie state 0' is published at once (no F-stubborn); (4) network: honest blocks reach the other honest nodes 10 s after being mined, pool-published blocks reach everyone instantly, honest blocks reach the pool instantly. Mining is memoryless, so one global exponential clock with mean INTERVAL is used and the finder is drawn in proportion to hash power (pool weight = round(100*alpha) of 100 equal miners).

HOW THE CLOSED PARAMETER SET IS USED (assumption): BLOCK_SIZE (otherwise unused here) is a mode code: 1 = Small + honest pool with the same 10 s delay (validation only), 3 = Small + L-stubborn, 4 = CA+Small + L-stubborn. CHURN_NODE_RATE (churn not modelled) carries alpha. NUM_OF_NODES=100, STDEV_OF_MINING_POWER=0, END_BLOCK_HEIGHT=100000 (stop when the public chain reaches it). t90_ms is meaningless here and is not used.

LIMITS: only L-stubborn alone, only Small and CA+Small (First-Seen out of scope); my L-stubborn is my reading of the paper's text and Nayak et al.'s state machine, since the authors' attacker code is unavailable; Fig.5 values are read off a chart (about +-0.01); the paper does not state how many seeds it averaged; ties between events at the same millisecond are resolved deterministically by queue order (delivery before mining), a modelling choice.

VALIDATION: honest mining gives the pool a revenue share equal to its hash share. With alpha=0.3 and 100,000 blocks, the std of one run's share is about 0.0015, so the mean of 3 seeds should be within 0.005 of 0.30 (the 0.005 allows the tiny advantage of a merged pool that never forks against itself).
title: Reproduce Fig.5 (L-stubborn, Small vs CA+Small) of the Common Ancestor paper in SimBlock, 100,000 blocks

validation.description: Known answer: with honest mining every miner earns revenue proportional to its hash power, so a pool with alpha=0.3 (mode 1: Smallest-Hash, pool behaves honestly, same 10 s delay as everyone) should have main-chain revenue share about 0.30 (paper Eq.1 and 'Ideally, an honest miner's revenue is proportional to its hash power'). The metric orphan_rate here is the redefined attacker revenue share.
